text:
incident-bot: PagerDuty alert: unusual sso-heartbeat spike from 3 IPs in APAC (count=18k/min). Auto-created channel #inc-9123456789
alice_sre: seeing increased 401/429 spikes across auth proxies, starting to trace.
bob_oncall: joining — oncall slot, what's the customer impact? :pager:
alice_sre: user-facing login errors up ~4% for enterprise customers in APAC, some repro with idp redirect failures
carla_sec: flagged as potential credential stuffing or log forward leakage. any logs showing tokens in clear?
dave_csr: two customers (AcmeCorp, Pixly) reported higher auth failures and support tickets, notifying them we are investigating
bob_oncall: can we throttle the 3 source IPs at the edge and add WAF rule? I can push IP block now.
frank_infra: I have ACLs ready, blocking 203.0.113.45/32, 198.51.100.12/32, 198.51.100.13/32 — applying now
incident-bot: deploy-bot: ACL update applied to edge NGINX (rev 7a4f) — 3 ips blocked
alice_sre: spike dropped by ~70% after block, still seeing anomalous session creation attempts from other ASNs
carla_sec: to be safe, rotate SSO client secrets for staging and prod service-accounts that touch the idp callback endpoint. Let's prioritize prod.
bob_oncall: agree. What's the list? frank, can you enumerate service accounts calling /auth/callback?
frank_infra: pulling list: `svc-auth-proxy`, `svc-webhook-ingest`, `svc-session-mgr` — prod versions v2.1.3
frank_infra: initiating secret rotation for svc-auth-proxy first. ETA ~6m
alice_sre: also found a misconfigured logshipper group forwarding raw auth headers to third-party sandbox — investigating if tokens were exported
carla_sec: that's the major concern. if raw headers were logged externally we need immediate erasure request and rotate keys.
erin_legal: if logs were forwarded off-network, we need to start a preservation and customer notification assessment. Please capture scope (which tenants) ASAP.
dave_csr: AcmeCorp and Pixly again show up in the forwarded log subset, both enterprise customers. Raising customer-impact flag.
frank_infra: rotation completed for svc-auth-proxy. Secrets updated in KMS and Deploy.
incident-bot: job-runner: secret-rotate svc-auth-proxy succeeded (job id 0x4f7a)
alice_sre: rolling restart auth-proxy clusters to pick up secrets. watch for 502s
bob_oncall: standby on 502s. traffic should fallback; rolling had no user impact so far.
carla_sec: next steps: (1) confirm whether any auth tokens escaped in third-party logs (2) rotate any leaked secret scopes (3) coordinate customer notice if PII or tokens exposed
alice_sre: query pattern that showed raw headers:
```
GET /auth/callback?code=... HTTP/1.1
Host: idp.redwood.example
Authorization: Bearer eyJhbGciOiJI...
```
carla_sec: initial grep shows ~420 lines in forwarded index matching `Authorization: Bearer` between 2026-03-16T01:12 and 2026-03-16T01:26 UTC
frank_infra: forwarding partner confirms logs were delivered to their ephemeral bucket, they've deleted the batch but we need written confirmation
frank_infra: emailing ops@partner with deletion request and asking for MD5+timestamp proof
erin_legal: please request full audit trail and retention policy from partner. preserve all internal logs related to the incident.
dave_csr: I've started drafting a customer-facing note: "We've detected anomalous auth traffic and rotated service credentials; we're investigating potential log forwarding — more detail to follow." Do we want to pre-notify AcmeCorp account security? :phone: 
carla_sec: yes, pre-notify as sensitive. Include mitigation steps and that tokens may have been in logs; advise them to rotate any tokens they control that rely on our SSO integration.
alice_sre: checking for abnormal token exchange counts: found 12 refresh tokens exchanged from same UA string likely bot-driven, timestamps align with forwarded logs
bob_oncall: ok rotate svc-session-mgr next. frank to rotate keys, alice to restart.
frank_infra: rotating svc-session-mgr now
incident-bot: pagerduty: alert acked by bob_oncall at 2026-03-16T01:35:10Z
frank_infra: svc-session-mgr rotation complete
alice_sre: restarted, healthchecks green
carla_sec: can we also revoke any short-lived session tokens issued during window? We can invalidate by bumping session-key-version header. That will log everyone out — need customer impact call.
dave_csr: log out customers? AcmeCorp heavy service may be impacted. Suggest scoped invalidation for enterprise tenants we know are in logs first, then global if partner refuses full deletion.
erin_legal: get approval for customer notification wording. I will standby to join the call with account teams.
frank_infra: partner sent deletion confirmation and a retention policy excerpt, but not MD5. They're pulling the S3 access logs and will send in 30m
carla_sec: prepare incident timeline and potential indicators of compromise (IOC): IPs, UA string, timestamps, forwarded index ids
alice_sre: compiling timeline now — will paste once ready
bob_oncall: handing off to sec on-call @carla_sec for deeper triage. I'll stay on bridge for customer coordination.
carla_sec: taking over. creating task list and assigning owners. Thank you.
